issues.issue: The parenthetical defining B-4 Partners LLC is garbled ("(“Managers Fund and Manager each being referred to mdividually as a “Borrower”"), so the label attached to the second party is not cleanly stated. The joint-and-several designation is otherwise plain.

"Control" is defined as the power to direct management and policies "whether through the ownership of Stock, by contract, or otherwise," a general catch-all sitting against two enumerated means. The 10%/director/joint-venture deeming rules are then switched on only "for purposes of the definition of Eligible Notes Receivable and Section 7.13," leaving the term with two different reaches in the same instrument.

The definition closes with "together with any obligations undertaken or assumed relating thereto," an open-ended catch-all appended to two specifically described obligations of the Fund. What else counts as "relating thereto" is not bounded.

The three alternatives run from a FIRREA-compliant appraisal to anything "otherwise acceptable to Lender" to "an informal or unwritten estimate of value by Servicer," so the term has no fixed content. A dispute over what qualifies as an "Authorized Appraisal" would turn on which limb governs.

"Bank Product" is "any financial accommodation extended ... by a Bank Product Provider (other than pursuant to this Agreement) including" seven listed services, leaving the general phrase's reach against the specific list uncertain. Because Bank Product Obligations are secured, the boundary matters.

The definition makes "a Borrower" mean "each of and either of Fund and Manager," while Section 1.2 provides that in any financial covenant "Borrower" means Fund and its Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis. Which sense governs a given covenant is not always evident.

The grant is over "all property, including, without limitation, each of the following," but the twelve enumerated categories omit Real Property and Real Estate Owned even though clause (l) mentions Real Property only as proceeds. A court could be asked whether the general words or the enumerated list fixes the collateral pool.

The term is defined wholly by reference to an unattached extrinsic document, "the written policies, procedures and guidelines of Fund ... in the form delivered to Lender and approved by Lender prior to the Closing Date." Since eligibility, extensions and appraisals all turn on it, its content is contestable outside the four corners.

"Collections" means "all cash, checks, notes, instruments, and other items of payment," with an inclusion list (insurance proceeds, proceeds of cash sales, rental proceeds, tax refunds) that says nothing about proceeds of a sale or payoff of a Note Receivable. Whether such proceeds are "Collections" is left open by the general-versus-specific structure.

Section 2.6(a) separately requires payoff and sale proceeds of Notes Receivable to be routed to a Cash Management Account, which suggests those proceeds are not already captured by "Collections" in clause (ii) of that same subsection. The two readings of "Collections" cannot both be right.
